extracted.intended_audience: general educated readers interested in social reform, motherhood, child welfare, and public efficiency (mothers, social reformers, policymakers)
extracted.subtask_description: A set of normative standards and reform proposals concerning motherhood, child culture, social parentage, and related public-economy inefficiencies (calls for specialized child-care institutions, education of women, and conservation/reduction of public waste).

rubrics_metrics.name: Instinct is an inadequate guide for modern life and child-rearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Instinct is nothing but inherited habit; it dates a long way behind us and is never any guide in new conditions or an incentive to betterment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essay argues that instincts (self-preservation, sex, maternal instinct, combat) are useful in primitive conditions but fail for modern needs like diet, clothing, industry, science, art, education, religion, and morality. Therefore mothers must not rely on 'maternal instinct' alone but must use reason, education and learned skill in caring for children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human purpose is growth, improvement and progress (not merely instinctual ends)
rubrics_metrics.description: What we are really here for is Growth, Improvement, Progress—and we have a deep and UNIVERSAL instinct towards that, too; but little is said about it!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author contrasts the glorification of primal instincts (combat, sex, self-preservation) with the central human aim of growth; policy and education should reflect and foster improvement rather than vindicate merely 'the struggle'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mothers must supplement instinct with knowledge, freedom, wisdom and power
rubrics_metrics.description: The children of today need mothers of today, and they must begin to supplement their primitive impulse by the very fullest, highest, richest powers of the human intellect and the human heart—the real human heart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because modern conditions change rapidly and present needs beyond inherited habits, mothers require education, freedom, and social power to 'feed and teach and save' children; love alone is insufficient without these tools and social supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: New Motherhood — Standard 1: fullest development of the woman
rubrics_metrics.description: The fullest development of the woman, in all her powers, that she may be the better qualified for her duties of transmission by inheritance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Women should develop their talents and capacities (not be confined to 'femininity' alone) so they provide a richer inheritance to their children; personal development is framed as beneficial to child and race.

rubrics_metrics.name: New Motherhood — Standard 2: fullest education of the woman in her office and duty of right selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The fullest education of the woman in all plain truths concerning her great office, and in her absolute duty of right selection—measuring the man who would marry her by his fitness for fatherhood; and holding him to the highest standards in his duty thereto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective mothers should be taught the biological, social and moral responsibilities of parenthood; part of motherhood preparation is selecting a mate fit for fatherhood and insisting on high standards of paternal responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: New Motherhood — Standard 3: recognize child culture as a specialized art and life service
rubrics_metrics.description: Intelligent recognition that child culture is the greatest of arts, that it requires high specialization and life service, and the glad entrance upon this service of those women naturally fitted for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Child-rearing should be professionalized: certain persons, by talent and training, should devote their lives to child culture. This recognizes specialization rather than expecting every mother to be equally expert.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide specialized places and services for babies ('A Place for Babies')
rubrics_metrics.description: A specially prepared environment, a special service of those best fitted for the task, the accumulated knowledge which we can never have until such places and such service are given—we need A PLACE FOR BABIES—and our homes arranged in relation to such places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates institutions (nurseries, baby-centres) staffed by trained specialists and integrated with home life; such places will allow accumulation of child-care knowledge and improve early childhood conditions on a societal scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine personal mothering with social parentage
rubrics_metrics.description: For each child, the healthy body and mind; the warm, deep love and protecting care of its own personal mother: and for all children, the best provision possible from the united love and wisdom of our social parentage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ideal merges intimate maternal care with collective, organized child welfare—children should have both a devoted personal mother and access to social services, expertise and community care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social Motherhood / Social Parentage: collective responsibility for children
rubrics_metrics.description: The Child does not need sacrifice. It needs Wisdom and Freedom and Knowledge and Power. It needs Social Motherhood—the conscious, united Mother Love and Mother Care of the Whole World.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rather than leaving child welfare to isolated individual mothers, society should organize collective, conscious care (education, public health, institutions) to protect and nurture all children; mothers should be supported by social structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject the doctrine of exclusive individual maternal devotion; recognize women's differentiated social roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Disagreeing with the demand for primitive motherhood—the entire devotion of each and every mother to her own children—on the ground that this method is not the best for child service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Women are individuals with varying talents and social roles; allowing women economic independence and opportunities for social service makes them better mothers and improves the home atmosphere for children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educate girls about the realities and duties of parenthood before marriage
rubrics_metrics.description: A girl old enough to marry, is old enough to understand thoroughly what lies before her and why. Women should recognize not only the personal joy of motherhood but the social duty of motherhood and its unmeasured powers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Premarital education in biological, social and parenting truths is both practical and moral: informed selection of mates and conscious acceptance of parenthood duties will improve race and reduce social ills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce dishonest and unnecessary public expenditures
rubrics_metrics.description: Recent spasms of civic investigation have revealed one large source of waste in the dishonest use of public money. We are taxed more than is necessary to meet expenses in no way essential to good government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Civic oversight and financial expertise (e.g., a Social Secretary and a Financial Expert) are proposed to curb corruption and waste in public finances—estimate given as about 10% lost to dishonest use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conserve natural resources to prevent large economic losses
rubrics_metrics.description: We waste largely in carelessness of our natural resources: waste of timber is followed by waste of water, and that by waste of land; the earth's surface of arable soil is being washed into the ocean at a wholly unnecessary rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy should prioritize soil conservation, forest and water management and harbor maintenance to prevent long-term loss of productive wealth—author suggests ~10% of wealth lost by such waste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recover and reuse urban sewage and garbage as valuable resources
rubrics_metrics.description: The waste of sewage in almost every city ... and the loss of the same valuable fertilizing material in smaller places, is grotesquely foolish. The sale of this material by any great city, together with the sale of its garbage, would be a large and steady source of income.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cities should process and sell sewage and garbage as fertilizer and raw material; doing so would save money, reduce dredging and health costs, and recover resources—estimated ~10% savings if addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent production of large defective/crippled/criminal populations through social measures
rubrics_metrics.description: We pay very heavily to support our public institutions for the defective, crippled and criminal population ... Practically all this is pure waste of money—the born criminal belongs in the hospital or asylum. Our criminal population is made—not born!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on prevention (better parenthood, public health, social conditions) rather than only on costly institutional support; reducing incidence would cut public expense and human suffering—estimated saving ~10%.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce disease and infant mortality by improving living conditions and public health
rubrics_metrics.description: Our all too numerous diseases with their premature deaths constitute another heavy loss. The waste of human life force in the infant mortality alone is enormous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public health measures, better housing, nutrition and maternal/child care would lower disease costs and preserve productive life—another suggested ~10% of wealth lost to disease and mortality that could be mitigated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce losses from fire, industrial and transportation accidents
rubrics_metrics.description: We lose by fire, unnecessarily, other huge sums ... In this, and in the terrible death roll from accident in mill and mine and railroad, we lose in money more than another ten per cent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in safety, building standards, accident prevention to save lives and economic value; these are uncompensated losses (no 'come back').

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid wasteful fragmentation and misdirected competition; better match occupations to people
rubrics_metrics.description: In the foolishness of throat-cutting competition ... we lose; in the general inadequacy of our people—low grade people where we might have high grade ones ... we waste again good ten per cent. Also in the blind, careless assortment of occupation where people work grudgingly at what they do not like we lose largely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Economic organization should reduce redundant competition, encourage specialization and place workers where they fit and are happy to increase productive output and reduce waste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce household/domestic industry waste (major source of living expense)
rubrics_metrics.description: Then comes our method of domestic industry in which we waste forty-three per cent. of the productive labor of the world—and three-fourths of our living expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improvements in household organization, tools, services (e.g., 'c. f. d.'—cooked food delivery, institutions for childcare) would dramatically cut domestic labor waste and living costs; collective solutions are implied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Women’s equality will not harm men; it will improve civilization and motherhood
rubrics_metrics.description: In the change from the dominance of one sex to the equal power of two ... No harm. The woman, free at last, intelligent, recognizing her real place and responsibility ... will be not less, but more, efficient as a mother.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essay argues equality of the sexes will enhance social selection for parenthood and allow women to make better choices for the race; men lose little, society gains through better parenthood practices.
